entities.name: Rolandino of Padua
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rolandino of Padua (c. 1200–1276), a distinguished Italian jurist, chronicler, and educator, stands as a pivotal figure in 13th-century intellectual history, primarily remembered for his foundational legal treatise, the *Summa totius artis notariae*, and his invaluable historical work, the *Chronica Marchiae Tarvisinae*. Educated and later teaching at the burgeoning University of Padua, Rolandino provided both practical legal guidance that shaped notarial practice across medieval Italy and a vivid, if partisan, eyewitness account of the tumultuous political landscape of the Veneto, particularly the brutal tyranny of Ezzelino III da Romano.

His *Summa totius artis notariae*, completed around 1255, rapidly became a standard textbook for notaries and jurists, offering comprehensive instruction on drafting legal documents, contracts, and wills. This work synthesized existing legal traditions and introduced practical innovations, standardizing complex procedures and ensuring consistency in a period of rapidly evolving communal law. Concurrently, his *Chronica Marchiae Tarvisinae*, covering the years 1200–1262, meticulously details the political, social, and military events in the March of Treviso. It is a crucial primary source for understanding the rise and fall of Ezzelino III da Romano, whose cruel reign (1237–1259) profoundly impacted the region, providing a unique perspective from someone deeply embedded in the communal life of Padua.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rolandino of Padua significantly shaped medieval legal practice through his widely adopted *Summa totius artis notariae* and provided an indispensable primary source for the political history of 13th-century Italy with his *Chronica Marchiae Tarvisinae*, influencing both legal and historical scholarship for centuries.
